newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: GTE executive among dead in Guatemala air crash.
newsitem.headline: GTE executive among dead in Guatemala air crash.

text.p: Five people including Bruce Haddad, the senior vice president of international operations for GTE Corp, and his wife died on Wednesday in a plane crash south of Guatemala City, aviation officials said.

"I called Peru (where the Haddads were picked up) to confirm the list of passengers, who were Bruce Haddad and Mrs Dorothy Haddad," Ronald Peter Zineri, Guatemala's director of civil aviation, told Reuters, adding that three Venezuelan crew members also were killed.
The corporate jet, a Westwind 24 chartered from the Venezuelan company Inversiones Liftoff, slammed into the side of a mountain about 3:30 a.m. (0930 GMT), Zineri said.
"It was good weather, 9 kilometres (5.6 miles) visibility, the tower told the pilot, and it's on tape, a few seconds before the accident that he was off course," Zineri said.
The crew was identified as pilot Carlos Izquierdo, Francisco Nieto and Rafael Ramon.
The plane had taken off from Caracas, Venezuela, picked up the Haddads in Lima, Peru, and was to make a stop in Guatemala City on its way to Dallas, Texas, officials said.
